title: LLM tutor panel shows zero feedback until the response (or 10s timeout) arrives — popup opens only after the await
evidence: In every branch the function builds the card, calls _llm_tutor.explain(_state), then `var result: Array = await _llm_tutor.explanation_ready`, and only AFTER the await calls `_open_popup(card["panel"])` (line 664). The 'Mrs. K is thinking…' label is added to a popup that is not yet visible. Verified live: an LLM answer takes ~2.2s; on error/timeout the child stares at the unchanged street for up to 10s after tapping ❓.
detail: The 2026-07-31 amendment puts a real network call behind the child-initiated '?' button. On the LLM path the child gets no immediate reaction to the tap — no popup, no spinner — which reads as a broken button to an 8-year-old and invites repeat taps (see related stale-timer note). The scripted-only path (no API key) is unaffected because there is no await.
recommended_fix: Call _open_popup(card["panel"]) immediately after building the card (before explain()), so 'Mrs. K is thinking…' is visible during the await; optionally disable the ❓ button while a call is in flight.

title: Touch targets fall short of the Always boundary's ≥2cm at phone widths
location: game/scenes/street.tscn (HUD buttons lines 65/72/79: 72×72 and 60×72; DominantButton line 114: 130px high) and game/scripts/street.gd (_make_big_button: 100px; asset OPEN/FIX: 140×96; leaderboard NEW GAME: 64px)
evidence: Viewport is 720×1280 logical with stretch canvas_items (project.godot). Mapped onto a ~7cm-wide portrait phone screen, 1 logical px ≈ 0.1mm, so 2cm ≈ 200 logical px. Largest control (DominantButton) is 130px ≈ 1.3cm; popup action buttons 100px ≈ 1.0cm; 🏆/❓ HUD buttons 72px ≈ 0.7cm; 🐞 60px; NEW GAME 64px.
detail: The frozen 'Always' boundary states 'icon-first labels ≤3 words on ≥2cm touch targets'. The ≤3-word half passes everywhere (FIND WORK, BUY, WORK SHIFT, NEW NAME, THAT'S IT, ACCEPT LIFE, FIX, OPEN, CLOSE…). The ≥2cm half is not met by any control at phone widths; only on a desktop window at native 720px (~19cm at 96 DPI) do the 100px+ buttons exceed 2cm.
recommended_fix: Raise minimum sizes in logical px for the 720-wide portrait: HUD buttons ≥96–104px square, popup/action buttons ≥130px high, remove the 64px NEW GAME exception (or relocate reset out of the kid path). Record the chosen logical-px-per-cm assumption in the playtest script so the gate can verify on a real device.

title: Stale one-shot timeout timer can cancel a subsequent in-flight LLM call
evidence: `get_tree().create_timer(TIMEOUT_SECONDS).timeout.connect(_on_timeout, CONNECT_ONE_SHOT)` keeps no per-call handle; _on_timeout only checks `_busy`. Sequence: call A completes in 2s (timer still pending), call B starts at 3s, A's timer fires at 10s → _busy is true (for B) → B's HTTPRequest is cancelled and B finishes as 'timeout' fallback after only ~7s, using a timer that belonged to A.
detail: Reachable because the ❓ HUD button stays tappable while a previous explanation is in flight (compounded by the popup-after-await issue). Impact is benign (scripted fallback, logged) but produces spurious fallbacks exactly when a curious kid double-taps — and the 10s budget promised per call is silently shortened.
recommended_fix: Capture a call generation (e.g. increment a counter, pass it to the timeout lambda and no-op if stale) or keep a Timer reference and stop it in _finish().

title: Corrupt-save path resets cleanly but skips the matrix's 'Log' step
evidence: load_game() returns {ok:false, corrupted:true} silently (no push_warning/print/log write), and _load_or_new_game() shows the apology beat and starts fresh. The other three required behaviors are verified by test_corrupt_save_keeps_street_name (133/133 green): fresh street, street name kept via finlit_street_name.txt, apology toast, no crash.
detail: The I/O & edge-case matrix row specifies 'Log + reset; never crash'. Only the log is missing — a parent/dev reviewing the prototype has no trace that a corruption occurred or how often it happens in playtests.
recommended_fix: push_warning (or append one line to a small user:// log) in load_game() when corrupted=true is detected, including the parse error if any.

title: First-purchase nudge fires on affordability, not on the tick
evidence: The 'savings_ready' teach beat fires once, only when `job != "" and assets.is_empty() and balance >= cheapest_asset_price()`. A market tick with no assets produces income $0 (verified) but no prompt of any kind; a kid below $40 with no assets gets no nudge toward saving/first purchase from the tick path.
detail: The matrix row 'TICK, no assets → income $0; prompt nudges first purchase' is arguably satisfied in spirit (a nudge exists and the dominant button glows BUY when affordable), but strictly the prompt is decoupled from the tick. Worth confirming at the playtest gate that the affordability-gated nudge plus glowing button is enough pull for a 9-year-old.
recommended_fix: Either accept and annotate the interpretation in the playtest script, or add a gentle periodic beat on ticks while asset-less (e.g. every Nth tick: 'Save up — $X to your first building').

title: Documented run commands fail on a fresh clone until an import pass; spec Verification command is invalid
evidence: With game/.godot deleted (fresh-clone simulation), `godot --headless --path game` exits with dozens of 'Could not find type LocalJsonBackend / FinLitEconomy …' parse errors because the global class cache does not exist yet. Running `godot --headless --path game --import` first regenerates it, after which the scene launches cleanly and tests pass 133/133. The spec's manual check `godot --headless --check-only game/project.godot` is not a valid invocation (--check-only pairs with --script, and project.godot is not accepted positionally).
detail: Anyone following the docs literally on a fresh checkout (e.g. Moses on another machine for the playtest) hits a wall of parse errors on first run. The project itself is fine — this is the standard Godot first-import requirement — but the docs should say so.
recommended_fix: Add to docs/playtest-script.md and the spec Verification: first run on a fresh clone requires `godot --headless --path game --import` (or opening the editor once); fix or replace the --check-only command.

title: Showroom leg of VISIBLE is not in the slice — visibility is street + fake leaderboard only
location: spec Intent ('VISIBLE (street + showroom)'); implementation: game/scripts/street.gd street render + _show_leaderboard()
evidence: Assets are NAMED (generator-first), PERSISTENT (JSON autosave), UPGRADEABLE (3 visible levels — icon grows 40+22·level px, ★ display) and VISIBLE on the street. Nothing implements a showroom/visit view: the leaderboard shows only the YOU row's climbed number, never the street itself. Multiplayer/sharing is correctly absent (Never list).
detail: For an offline single-player slice this is the only sensible reading — the fake leaderboard is the SHOW stub and the spec task list never scheduled a showroom. Recorded so the deferred leg is explicit rather than silently dropped from the formula.
recommended_fix: No code change for this slice; note 'showroom deferred to server phase (Marcus canned-visit per brainstorm)' in the spec Design Notes or next-iteration list.

title: LLM answers can contain markdown that renders literally in the kid-facing Label
location: game/scripts/street.gd _show_tutor_panel() (plain Label, no BBCode); observed via game/tests/test_llm_live.gd live run
evidence: Live DeepSeek run (2026-07-31, source=llm, 2226ms) returned '- **WORK SHIFT** means you work…' and '- **BUY Stock Tower** costs your $40…' — the ** markers will render as literal asterisks in the plain Godot Label shown to the child. Word cap held (79 ≤ 80) and content was on-persona, so this is cosmetic.
detail: The 80-word cap, persona lock, scope lock and fallback all verified live; only output formatting leaks model markup into kid-visible text.
recommended_fix: Strip common markdown tokens (**, *, #, leading '- ') in trim_to_word_cap or a small sanitizer before display, or add 'no markdown, plain sentences' to the system prompt HARD RULES.

title: Call attempts that never reach the network are not written to the parent jsonl log
location: game/scripts/llm_tutor.gd explain() — early returns for !is_available() and _busy emit the fallback without append_log(); only _finish() logs
evidence: explain() returns early (deferred emit, no log entry) when DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is absent or a call is already in flight. append_log() is only reached via _finish(), i.e. after an actual request was attempted. Verified: the jsonl contains only the real network call from the live run.
detail: The amendment asks for a 'parent-reviewable jsonl log' of the LLM rig. Attempts where the child tapped ❓ and got the scripted fallback without any network attempt leave no trace, so a parent reviewing the log undercounts how often the child asked for help. Low stakes in the prototype, but it is the parent-trust surface.
recommended_fix: Log a lightweight entry (source='scripted'/'busy_fallback', no request payload) on the two early-return paths too.

title: Burst-pipe card drawn with no valid target produces an unexplained thud and no beat
evidence: When the only assets are stocks (or everything is already damaged), _draw_event can still select burst_pipe, which returns effect='no_target'. street.gd's match has branches only for no_debt/interest_charged/damaged, so the kid hears _sfx.thud() and sees no card or text. Covered by test ('stocks can't flood -> no target') as intended logic, but the UI side is a silent no-op.
detail: Not a matrix violation (no row covers a target-less disaster), but a confusing juice moment: a consequence sound with no consequence. The spec design notes promise a teach beat per event ('one-line consequence narration').
recommended_fix: Skip the thud for no_target events, or show a tiny beat ('Storm passed — nothing to flood!'). Cheapest: only play thud inside the matched branches.

title: AC2 and AC3 are playtest-observed by definition and remain unverified until the playtest gate runs
location: spec Acceptance Criteria rows 2–3; docs/playtest-script.md (protocol ready, unfilled)
evidence: AC2 (kid states what a disaster cost THEIR building, observed in playtest) and AC3 (9-year-old unaided: ≥2 assets, 1 upgrade, 1 event survived, asks to play again tomorrow) cannot be evidenced from code. docs/playtest-script.md is complete and maps every criterion to an observation checkbox, but no filled results exist in the repo. AC1's mechanics are verified by design (first wage lands immediately on job pick — _wage_timer primed to WAGE_DROP_SECONDS; all action labels ≤3 words) and by unit tests, pending only the stopwatch at the gate.
detail: Spec status 'in-review' is consistent: the playtest with Moses' kid is iteration step 1 and is the gate. Recorded so the review does not read the three [x]-adjacent criteria as code-verified.
recommended_fix: Run docs/playtest-script.md before merging past the gate; file the filled scorecard alongside the spec (and feed the reroll-policy, no-parents-tone and LLM-vs-scripted evidence lines back into canon).
